# paindrawr ![paindrawr package logo](reference/figures/paindrawr-logo.png)

**paindrawr** is an R package for analysing and visualising pain
drawings — illustrations on which patients indicate where they
experience pain. Pain drawings typically use a full-body outline but can
also focus on specific anatomical regions.

The package provides tools to import pain drawing data, visualise the
marked areas, and quantify pain location, distribution, and extent. This
allows researchers to turn patient-reported pain drawings into
quantitative data for statistical analysis.

Pain drawings have traditionally been scored by dividing the body into a
fixed set of anatomical regions and recording, for each region, whether
it was marked or not. Modern digital tools (web and tablet apps) instead
capture each drawing as a series of pen-stroke *x/y coordinates*. This
coordinate-based data is far richer, but it is also harder to work with.
paindrawr provides a consistent workflow for turning that raw coordinate
data into figures and quantitative summaries.

## Installation

You can install the development version of paindrawr from
[GitHub](https://github.com/steenharsted/paindrawr) with:

``` r

pak::pak("steenharsted/paindrawr")
```

## Collect with paindraw. Analyse with paindrawr.

![paindraw and paindrawr
logos](reference/figures/paindraw_and_paindrawr.png)

**paindraw** is a REDCap external module for collecting digital pain
drawings.

**paindrawr** is an R package for importing, quantifying, analysing, and
visualising pain drawings.

Together, they provide a workflow from digital data collection to
research-ready results.

## Typical workflow

paindrawr functions are organised around a common analysis pipeline:

1.  **Import** raw drawings:
    [`pdr_import_json()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_import_json.md),
    [`pdr_import_png()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_import_png.md)
2.  **Check** that the data is well-formed:
    [`pdr_match()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_match.md)
3.  **Rasterise** the strokes to an RGBA array with
    [`pdr_add_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_add_rgba.md).
    Choose `polygon = "none"` to keep strokes as drawn, or `"pen"`,
    `"spray"` or `"both"` to render them as filled polygons.
4.  **Quantify** the marked areas:
    [`pdr_summarize_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_summarize_rgba.md)
5.  **Visualise** the results:
    [`pdr_plot_xy()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_xy.md),
    [`pdr_plot_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_rgba.md),
    [`pdr_plot_rgba_heatmap()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_rgba_heatmap.md)

## Data structure

paindrawr works with a tibble in which each row is one respondent. The
pain drawings live in a dedicated list-column (named `pdr_data` by
default, but any name can be used), so that each drawing, with its
metadata, strokes and point coordinates, travels alongside covariates
such as sex, age, symptom duration or pain intensity.

The package ships with `pdr_example_data`, which has exactly this format
and is used throughout the documentation. See
[`?pdr_match`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_match.md)
for the terminology (pdr_drawing, pdr_list, pdr_tibble).

## Example

The `pdr_*()` functions are designed to be used with the native pipe
(`|>`) alongside tidyverse verbs such as `mutate()` and
[`filter()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/filter.html).

``` r

library(paindrawr)
library(tidyverse)

pdr_example_data
#> # A tibble: 50 × 6
#>    id                               pdr_data          sex     age duration  pain
#>    <chr>                            <list>            <fct> <dbl> <fct>    <dbl>
#>  1 6d63804892233bbb18bc21bcf0d81d0d <named list [10]> Fema…  46   Chronic      6
#>  2 c8b12cd45d08e94241d4de9990d60f71 <named list [10]> Fema…  35.4 Acute        6
#>  3 25062ac7dbeb08d8b532ac474a7849ca <named list [10]> Fema…  38.4 Acute        5
#>  4 0dc657fa6ed70150f9596fe692f2f9a0 <named list [10]> Male   98   Subacute     3
#>  5 fb61c33ffa09270a5c7931813e9d2d71 <named list [10]> Fema…  58.3 Acute        1
#>  6 328d31503202db3e5c1b8e78f287810e <named list [10]> Male   68.9 Subacute     7
#>  7 e07d8d7e7034ba3ae7f907de022af58d <named list [10]> Fema…  67.4 Subacute     6
#>  8 9996f1a95c8e939c6ab6258bfc76f722 <named list [10]> Fema…  53.4 Chronic      9
#>  9 41aa308e694ad270b7cfaea054c7c1a2 <named list [10]> Fema…  36.8 Chronic      9
#> 10 0bcfd36a71b799e857f13c29011d21ff <named list [10]> Fema…  34.9 Subacute     4
#> # ℹ 40 more rows
```

The example data contains 50 respondents. Metadata stored inside each
drawing can be extracted with
[`pdr_get_info()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_get_info.md),
for example the canvas width:

``` r

pdr_example_data |>
  mutate(width = pdr_get_info(pdr_data, id1 = ".width"))
#> # A tibble: 50 × 7
#>    id                              pdr_data     sex     age duration  pain width
#>    <chr>                           <list>       <fct> <dbl> <fct>    <dbl> <int>
#>  1 6d63804892233bbb18bc21bcf0d81d… <named list> Fema…  46   Chronic      6   450
#>  2 c8b12cd45d08e94241d4de9990d60f… <named list> Fema…  35.4 Acute        6   450
#>  3 25062ac7dbeb08d8b532ac474a7849… <named list> Fema…  38.4 Acute        5   450
#>  4 0dc657fa6ed70150f9596fe692f2f9… <named list> Male   98   Subacute     3   450
#>  5 fb61c33ffa09270a5c7931813e9d2d… <named list> Fema…  58.3 Acute        1   450
#>  6 328d31503202db3e5c1b8e78f28781… <named list> Male   68.9 Subacute     7   450
#>  7 e07d8d7e7034ba3ae7f907de022af5… <named list> Fema…  67.4 Subacute     6   450
#>  8 9996f1a95c8e939c6ab6258bfc76f7… <named list> Fema…  53.4 Chronic      9   450
#>  9 41aa308e694ad270b7cfaea054c7c1… <named list> Fema…  36.8 Chronic      9   450
#> 10 0bcfd36a71b799e857f13c29011d21… <named list> Fema…  34.9 Subacute     4   450
#> # ℹ 40 more rows
```

### Plot a single drawing

[`pdr_plot_xy()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_xy.md)
redraws a drawing from its coordinates. Plots are easier to interpret
with the background image that was used during data collection; read
your own PNG with
[`png::readPNG()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/png/man/readPNG.html).

``` r

background <- png::readPNG(pdr_example_file("bg_full_body.png"))

pdr_example_data |>
  head(1) |>
  pdr_plot_xy(background_image = background)
```

![Example plot with background
image](reference/figures/README-plot-drawing-1.png)

Strokes can also be rendered as filled polygons, which is typically
sensible for pen tools (whereas spray tools produce many individual
points):

``` r

pdr_example_data |>
  head(1) |>
  pdr_plot_xy(background_image = background, polygon = "both")
```

![Example polygon plot with background
image](reference/figures/README-plot-polygon-1.png)

### Quantify drawings

Quantification and heatmaps work on a rasterised representation of each
drawing, added to the list-column with
[`pdr_add_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_add_rgba.md):

``` r

pd <- pdr_example_data |>
  mutate(pdr_data = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data, polygon = "both"))
```

[`pdr_summarize_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_summarize_rgba.md)
then computes summary statistics, such as the number of drawn pixels
(`px`) and the proportion of the canvas covered (`area_prop`):

``` r

pd |>
  pdr_summarize_rgba(summary_stat = c("px", "area_prop")) |>
  select(-pdr_data)
#> # A tibble: 50 × 7
#>    id                  sex     age duration  pain pdr_data_px pdr_data_area_prop
#>    <chr>               <fct> <dbl> <fct>    <dbl>       <int>              <dbl>
#>  1 6d63804892233bbb18… Fema…  46   Chronic      6        4232            0.0188 
#>  2 c8b12cd45d08e94241… Fema…  35.4 Acute        6       12782            0.0568 
#>  3 25062ac7dbeb08d8b5… Fema…  38.4 Acute        5        1287            0.00572
#>  4 0dc657fa6ed70150f9… Male   98   Subacute     3        6291            0.0280 
#>  5 fb61c33ffa09270a5c… Fema…  58.3 Acute        1         579            0.00257
#>  6 328d31503202db3e5c… Male   68.9 Subacute     7        3744            0.0166 
#>  7 e07d8d7e7034ba3ae7… Fema…  67.4 Subacute     6        3355            0.0149 
#>  8 9996f1a95c8e939c6a… Fema…  53.4 Chronic      9        3399            0.0151 
#>  9 41aa308e694ad270b7… Fema…  36.8 Chronic      9        1384            0.00615
#> 10 0bcfd36a71b799e857… Fema…  34.9 Subacute     4        2884            0.0128 
#> # ℹ 40 more rows
```

Supplying `stencils` (for example body regions) gives statistics per
region; see
[`?pdr_summarize_rgba`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_summarize_rgba.md).

### Heatmaps across groups

[`pdr_plot_rgba_heatmap()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_rgba_heatmap.md)
aggregates many drawings into density heatmaps, optionally stratified by
one or two grouping variables. Here we stratify by symptom duration:

``` r

pd |>
  pdr_plot_rgba_heatmap(
    variables = "duration",
    background_image = background
  )
```

![Heatmap](reference/figures/README-plot-heatmap-1.png)

## Importing your own data

``` r

# Drawings exported as JSON from the REDCap PainDraw module
pdr_import_json(list.files("path/to/json", full.names = TRUE))
```

See
[`?pdr_import_json`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_import_json.md)
and
[`?pdr_import_png`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_import_png.md)
for details.

# Package index

## Importing

Functions for importing data into paindrawr

- [`pdr_import_json()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_import_json.md)
  : Import RedCap PainDraw JSON data
- [`pdr_import_png()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_import_png.md)
  : Import PNG files as pdr drawings
- [`pdr_mird2pdr()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_mird2pdr.md)
  : Convert MIRD pain drawings to a pdr_list

## Plotting

Functions for Plotting data.

- [`pdr_plot_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_rgba.md)
  : Plot RGBA rasters in a grid
- [`pdr_plot_rgba_heatmap()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_rgba_heatmap.md)
  : Plot a pain heatmap from rendered RGBA rasters
- [`pdr_plot_stencil()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_stencil.md)
  : Plot stencil data
- [`pdr_plot_xy()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_xy.md)
  : Recreate a pain drawing as a ggplot

## Image quantification

- [`pdr_summarize_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_summarize_rgba.md)
  : Summarise the alpha values of drawn pixels in a pain drawing

## paindrawr data modification

- [`pdr_add_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_add_rgba.md)
  : Add an RGBA raster array to a pain drawing based on spray
  coordinates
- [`pdr_explode()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_explode.md)
  : Explode pain drawings into multiple drawings by stroke
- [`pdr_implode()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_implode.md)
  : Implode multiple pain drawings into one
- [`pdr_modify_points()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_modify_points.md)
  : Modify the points of pain drawings
- [`pdr_modify_rgba()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_modify_rgba.md)
  : Modify the rgba data of pain drawings

## Stencils

Premade stencils to aid in image analysis

- [`pdr_add_stencil()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_add_stencil.md)
  : Create and add a stencil to pain drawings.
- [`pdr_plot_stencil()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_plot_stencil.md)
  : Plot stencil data
- [`pdr_stencil_full_body`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_stencil_full_body.md)
  : Anatomical regions of the full body template, with stencils

## Example data

Example data and files

- [`pdr_example_data`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_example_data.md)
  : Example pain drawings with clinical variables
- [`pdr_example_file()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_example_file.md)
  : Local absolute path to example files
- [`pdr_example_geometry`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_example_geometry.md)
  : Example pain drawings with simple geometric cases

## Helper functions

- [`pdr_match()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_match.md)
  : Check or coerce pain drawing data types
- [`pdr_get_info()`](https://steenharsted.github.io/paindrawr/reference/pdr_get_info.md)
  : Extract information from pain drawing objects
